context.full_target:
Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
context.conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In addition E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0; no assertion at time zero is made.

record.definition: u_tt(x,t)=∂u_t(x,t)/∂t, the componentwise second time derivative.

record.type: spatial derivative matrix field on ℝ^n × (0,∞)
record.definition: D_xu has columns ∂_{x_j}u for j=1,...,n, with ∂_{x_j} the componentwise partial derivative in coordinate j; ∂_{x_jx_j}u denotes its second derivative in that coordinate. Derivatives of u_t use the same convention. Its Frobenius square is |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|².

e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Norms and dot products throughout are Euclidean; all spatial integrals are Lebesgue integrals, written dx. Write e_t for the time partial derivative of e.
E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx, the finite real Lebesgue integral, with exactly the normalization in the exercise (no factor 1/2).

b is integrable with respect to μ.

record.statement: For every t0>0, let J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. There exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n and R>0 such that C⊂(−R,R)^n and u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[−R,R]^n; Q has finite Lebesgue measure (2R)^n. All positive-order derivatives of u vanish on (ℝ^n∖C)×int J. For every r∈int J, each of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_tt(·,r), and, for j=1,...,n, ∂_{x_j}u(·,r)·∂_{x_j}u_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(·,r), and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u)(·,r) is continuous, zero outside C, bounded on Q and absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. In particular e(·,t) is integrable for every t>0. The fields e and e_t are jointly continuous on ℝ^n×(0,∞).
